instruction.name: xvldrepl.h
instruction.description: Read 16-bit data from memory address `addr + offset`, replicate the data to all vector lanes and save into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. The `offset` operand is a byte offset, matching the assembly immediate; the encoded instruction stores it as a scaled immediate for wider elements.

experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 6666 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 9 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; st.d $r0, $r20, 0; st.d $r0, $r20, 8' --asm 'xvldrepl.h $xr0, $r20, 0; xvpickve2gr.d $r4, $xr0, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'

latencies.notes: rj -> vd. Chain: xvldrepl.h reading at the carried base, then xvpickve2gr.d (6 cycles) and add.d (1 cycle) to advance the base; the 7-cycle closure is subtracted. L1D hit. Three independent runs, raw cycle spread 12.00-12.00. Measured on 2026-11-17 on LA464, core 0.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvldrepl.h $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.h $xr1, $r20, 2; xvldrepl.h $xr2, $r20, 4; xvldrepl.h $xr3, $r20, 6; xvldrepl.h $xr4, $r20, 8; xvldrepl.h $xr5, $r20, 10; xvldrepl.h $xr6, $r20, 12; xvldrepl.h $xr7, $r20, 14
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'xvldrepl.h $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.h $xr1, $r20, 2; xvldrepl.h $xr2, $r20, 4; xvldrepl.h $xr3, $r20, 6; xvldrepl.h $xr4, $r20, 8; xvldrepl.h $xr5, $r20, 10; xvldrepl.h $xr6, $r20, 12; xvldrepl.h $xr7, $r20, 14'

notes: L1D-hit vector load, 5 cycles from the base address register to the vector destination. The closure moves the loaded value to a GPR with a pick (3 cycles for vpickve2gr, 5 for xvpickve2gr) and advances the base with add.d, and a freshly loaded vector register reaches a cross-domain pick one cycle later than a vector ALU result does, which is the extra cycle the chain carries; the load itself is 5, the same number the scalar and integer loads take one step earlier. A vector load cannot feed an address, so there is no bypass case.
